label: Worm's Eye
clause: Plant the lens at dirt so the person becomes a tower, floorboards race toward a vanishing ceiling, and shoes are monuments.

label: Ground Level
clause: Set the lens on the ground plane so grit, weeds, and the first few inches of furniture own the foreground.

label: Ankle Height
clause: Ride at ankle height so socks, cuffs, and kicking dust are the closer story and faces are distant weather.

label: Hip Height
clause: Hold the lens at hip bone so belts, pockets, and swinging hands dominate, heads cut by the top edge.

label: Waist Height
clause: Place the lens at waist so tabletops, belt buckles, and midriffs are the horizon of the body.

label: Seated Eyeline
clause: Sit the lens at chair height so standing people loom and seated partners meet the lens honestly.

label: Tabletop Height
clause: Slide along tabletop height so plates, glasses, and elbows are mountains and faces rise beyond the spread.

label: Chest-Cam
clause: Mount at sternum height so the wearer's chin may clip the top and the world becomes a barreling corridor.

label: Eye Level
clause: Match a standing eyeline so the horizon cuts the ears and we meet the person as a peer.

label: High Standing
clause: Raise the lens a head above the person so the floor becomes a map and the crown becomes a dark oval.

label: Boom
clause: Boom the lens just above head height so hair partings and the tops of lamps enter, the floor falling away.

label: Bird's Eye
clause: Survey steeply from tree or mast height, keeping a sliver of horizon so the place becomes a model but not a plan.

label: Nadir
clause: Point the lens straight at pavement so heads are disks and shadows are attached coins.

label: Zenith
clause: Point the lens straight at the sky so a ceiling rose, weather, or canopy is the only map, no horizon at all.

label: Front
clause: Face the person square so both ears hint at the edges and the gaze hits the glass.

label: Three-Quarter Left
clause: Stand off the closer cheek so the distant ear hides and a window behind that shoulder blooms as a panel of sky.

label: Three-Quarter Right
clause: Park beside the jawline so the closer shoulder leads like a prow and a corridor recedes behind the hidden ear.

label: Profile Left
clause: Turn to a full side view so the nose-to-nape silhouette cuts the pane and one eye becomes a single gleam.

label: Profile Right
clause: Hold the opposite side-on cut so the mouth's corner and the nape hairline are the only face that exists.

label: Three-Quarter Back Left
clause: Work behind the closer scapula so the cheek becomes a sliver and the world they face is mostly withheld.

label: Three-Quarter Back Right
clause: Hide behind the distant shoulder blade so we steal a slice of jaw and the view they own stays secret.

label: Behind
clause: Sit on the nape so we follow the back of the head, ears, and the world they walk into.

label: OTS Left
clause: Peek past a living shoulder so the distant face is nested in the crook of neck and cloth.

label: OTS Right
clause: Rest the lens against a collar and scapula mass so the distant talker has to climb out of a dark wedge.

label: Point of View
clause: See as the person sees: their hands in the lower edge, the task or face they attend filling the center.

label: Reverse POV
clause: Turn around on the point-of-view so we see the looker's own face reacting to what we just saw.

label: Through Window
clause: Shoot through glass so reflections of the street layer over the interior scene.

label: Through Foliage
clause: Part leaves in the foreground field so the scene becomes a peephole of chlorophyll and sun flecks.

label: Through Fence
clause: Shoot through chain or palings so the world is striped and the person is caged by the occluder.

label: Under Table
clause: Slide under a table so undersides of wood, knees, and hanging hands are the architecture.

label: Over Furniture
clause: Shoot over a sofa back or chair so upholstery becomes a foreground wall and faces sit in the remaining slot.

label: Mild Dutch
clause: Tip the horizon a few degrees so doorframes lean like a hint of unease while furniture still reads usable.

label: Heavy Dutch
clause: Cant the world until floor becomes a slide and lamp posts cut the pane as diagonals.

label: Snap Dutch
clause: Jolt the horizon off-level in one accent so the room feels struck, not gradually leaned.

label: Level Horizon
clause: Lock the horizon true so verticals of the tower stand and the floor becomes a reliable plane.

label: Drone 45 Orbit
clause: Orbit at a forty-five-degree downward angle so the building turns as a faceted object against the bay.

label: Drone Top-Down
clause: Hover at altitude so rooftops, trees, and a tiny walker form a living map.

label: Drone High Oblique
clause: Hold a steep oblique so both facade and roof read, the place as a three-dimensional block.

label: Ridge Reveal
clause: Rise over a ridge or parapet so the hidden plaza blooms into view past stone.

label: Periscope
clause: Peek over a wall or dashboard with a periscope optic so the body of the rig is hidden and only the distant table appears.

label: Helmet Cam
clause: Ride inside a visor so the rim of the helmet becomes a dark arch and the next obstacle fills the center.

label: Dash Cam
clause: Lock to a dashboard looking through the windscreen so wipers, hood, and the road's vanishing point own the pane.

label: CCTV High Corner
clause: Park in a ceiling corner looking diagonally so the room becomes a wedge of floor, slightly cold and supervisory.

label: Low Hero
clause: Kneel so the figure towers, ceiling recedes, and the jawline becomes a cliff against sky.

label: God's Eye
clause: Hold a plan view of a whole room or plaza as if a diagram, furniture readable as icons around a body.

label: Kanted Conversation
clause: Cant the two-shot of a conversation so both people share a tipped floor and the talk feels unstable.

label: Sumo
clause: Squat at belt-buckle height with a sense of weight, the torso a monument and the head against ceiling.

label: Kneeling
clause: Kneel at a child's standing eyeline so adult hands hang huge and faces tilt into the pane.

label: Balcony
clause: Shoot from a balcony rail so the street becomes a drop and the railing becomes a closer-field bar.

label: Mezzanine
clause: Stand on a mezzanine looking along the rail so the floor below becomes a theater of small people.

label: Through Blinds
clause: Shoot through slats so the scene arrives in stripes of bright and denied.

label: Door Crack
clause: Peer through a barely open door so a slice of the next room is all we are allowed.

label: Crowd Gap
clause: Steal a view through a gap in a crowd so shoulders are curtains and the distant event becomes a postage stamp.

label: Underwater Up
clause: Aim from underwater so the surface becomes a bright ceiling of waves and legs are columns.

label: Orchestra Pit
clause: Sit in a pit aiming at a stage lip so performers are giants above a dark well.

label: Rafters
clause: Hang in the rafters so trusses and dust are the closer field and people below are small moving parts.

label: Fire Escape
clause: Shoot from a fire-escape landing so iron stairs stripe the pane and the alley drops away.

label: Rooftop Edge
clause: Stand at a rooftop lip looking along the cornice so the street becomes a thin canyon.

label: Basement Stairs
clause: Aim up a basement stair so the doorway at the top becomes a bright rectangle of the world above.

label: Top of Stairs
clause: Stand at the top aiming down the well so banisters recede and the landing becomes a destination.

label: Bottom of Stairs
clause: Stand at the bottom aiming so the climber approaches as a silhouette against an upper window.

label: Ladder
clause: Cling to a ladder so rungs are a grid and the climber's boots or the sky alternate as the prize.

label: Scaffold
clause: Ride scaffolding so pipes and couplings cage the facade being worked.

label: Dock Waterline
clause: Set the lens at the waterline of a dock so planks, reflections, and hulls share one plane.

label: Pool Edge
clause: Rest at pool coping so water becomes a sheet in the lower pane and a figure stands on the distant lip.

label: Opposite Bank
clause: Shoot from the opposite bank so a river or road becomes a barrier and the person becomes a small distant event.

label: Cliff
clause: Perch on a cliff so the drop is the foreground and the figure is tiny against geology.

label: Mountain Saddle
clause: Sit in a mountain saddle so two valleys open on either side and a walker becomes a speck on the pass.

label: Canyon Floor
clause: Stand on a canyon floor so walls rise like a slot and sky becomes a thin ribbon.

label: Train Platform
clause: Hold a platform eyeline so the track pit becomes a trench and arriving cars fill the distant plane.

label: Bus Bench
clause: Sit at bench height on a curb so passing wheels are huge and waiting legs share the pane.

label: Counter Height
clause: Rest on a service counter so goods and elbows are the closer field and the clerk's torso rises beyond.

label: One-Way Glass
clause: Shoot through observation glass so the watched room becomes a diorama and a faint reflection of watchers ghosts the pane.

label: Skylight
clause: Aim through a skylight so the interior becomes a lit box seen through a roof aperture.

label: Floor Grate
clause: Aim through a grate so shoes and a slice of sky are checkered by metal.

label: Bookshelf Aisle
clause: Stand in a stack aisle so unmarked spines wall both sides and a face waits at the vanishing point.

label: Under Umbrella
clause: Shoot from under an umbrella so fabric becomes a canopy and rain stitches the world beyond the rim.

label: Coat Hood
clause: Ride inside a hood so fabric tunnels the view and the street becomes a bright oval.

label: Wing Mirror
clause: Use a wing-mirror as the view so the world is reversed in a small glass and the road behind is the owner.

label: Loading Dock
clause: Stand at truck-bed height on a dock so bumpers, bays, and a worker's knees share the plane.

label: Clock Tower
clause: Shoot from a tower opening so the square below becomes a diagram of paths and the clock mechanism may clip the edge.

label: Wheelchair Height
clause: Ride at wheelchair height so doorknobs, tabletops, and standing thighs are the architecture of the room.

label: Child Height
clause: Stand at a small child's eyeline so tabletops are ceilings and adult faces require a tilt.

label: Supine
clause: Lie on the back aiming so a face leaning over us is an eclipse against ceiling.

label: Cabinet
clause: Shoot from inside a cabinet or fridge so the door-frame becomes a proscenium and the kitchen becomes a bright stage.

label: Back Seat
clause: Sit in a back seat aiming forward so headrests are columns and the driver's nape is the closer owner.

label: Handlebar
clause: Mount at handlebar height so grips, stem, and the rushing road are the whole world.

label: Across the Street
clause: Hold from across the street so parked cars and a lane of asphalt are the moat before the doorway.

label: Loft
clause: Shoot from a loft or sleeping platform so the room below becomes a well and beams cut the upper pane.

label: Pulpit
clause: Stand at a pulpit looking out so pews recede as a congregation diagram.

label: Pew
clause: Sit in a pew aiming forward so heads and a distant speaker are the axis of the hall.

label: Ticket Booth
clause: Shoot from inside a booth so the window shelf, a speaking hole, and the queue beyond are the set.

label: Kitchen Pass
clause: Aim through a pass-through so steam, plates, and the dining room are stacked in a rectangular slot.

label: Closet
clause: Shoot from inside a closet so hanging clothes are curtains and the bedroom becomes a bright crack.

label: Under Bed
clause: Slide under a bed so slats, dust, and shoes at the edge are the architecture.

label: Catwalk
clause: Track an industrial catwalk so grate floor and a drop to machinery open on both sides.

label: Elevator Corner
clause: Park in an elevator corner so the door, floor indicator, and packed bodies are a box of reflections.

label: Doorbell Height
clause: Stand at doorbell height so the door fills the pane like a wall and a face will appear in the spyhole zone.

label: Stair Landing
clause: Occupy a landing so two flights split the pane, one rising, one falling.

label: Between Cars
clause: Stand between parked cars so mirrors and flanks make a corridor toward a crosswalk.

label: Crane Basket
clause: Ride a crane basket so the city becomes a drop and the rail of the basket becomes a closer bar.

label: Second Story
clause: Shoot from a second-story window so pedestrians are half-scale and shop awnings are roofs.

label: Forehead Height
clause: Raise just above the brow line so we aim slightly along the nose and the chest recedes.

label: Calf Height
clause: Ride at calf height so boots, a dog's eye-line, and furniture undersides own the closer field.

label: Over Monitor
clause: Shoot over a monitor lid so the screen's glow edges the chin of the person beyond.

label: Under-Chin Up
clause: Tilt from under the chin so the jaw becomes a cliff, nostrils a cave, and the ceiling a backdrop.

label: Behind Curtain
clause: Shoot through or from behind a curtain so fabric becomes a veil and the room becomes a muffled glow.

label: Rain Glass
clause: Shoot through rained glass so drops and rivulets break the street into beads.

label: Glass Floor
clause: Aim through a glass floor so the level below becomes a diorama underfoot.

label: Aisle
clause: Stand in a center aisle so symmetry pulls to an altar, desk, or screen at the distant plane.

label: Stage Wings
clause: Peek from stage wings so black masking gives way to lamps and an audience as a dark sea.

label: Security Wedge
clause: Hold a corner wedge like a security head, the room a surveyed diagram with no intimacy.

label: Drone Hover Front
clause: Hover in front at mid altitude so the facade becomes a flat elevation, neither plan nor worm.

label: Drone Hover Rear
clause: Hover behind the building so service alleys, vents, and the unpretty back are the rear elevation.

label: FPV Gap
clause: Thread a gap as if a flying lens so a doorway or railing lashes the edges.

label: Over Steering
clause: Shoot over a steering wheel so the rim, dashboard, and the road ahead share the pane.

label: Mezzanine Along
clause: Slide along a mezzanine rail aiming the length so the floor below travels under a banister.

label: Opposite Balcony
clause: Shoot from the balcony across a void so another balcony and its people are a diorama over air.

label: Altar
clause: Stand at an altar or dais aiming back so the hall becomes a receding vessel of seats.

label: Ditch
clause: Sit in a ditch or gutter so the road becomes a wall and wheels pass at eye height.

label: Rooftop Across
clause: Shoot from a neighboring roof so chimneys and the target building are a skyline conversation.

label: Vent
clause: Aim through a vent so slats stripe a slice of the next room.

label: Sunroof
clause: Aim through a sunroof so sky and passing branches are a moving ceiling.

label: Hatch
clause: Pop a roof hatch so the first view becomes a ring of roof and then the sky.

label: Between Shelves
clause: Squeeze so only a ribbon of a browsing face is allowed between two shelf edges.

label: Service Pit
clause: Aim from a service pit under a vehicle so undercarriage, oil, and boots at the rim are the sky.

label: Car Side Window
clause: Shoot through an open car side window so the door frame becomes a proscenium and the street slides.

label: Attic
clause: Shoot from attic boards so insulation, joists, and a knothole of the room below are the view.

label: Marina
clause: Hold from a slip so masts make a forest and hulls are the foreground street.

label: Bridge Span
clause: Stand mid-span so the road or river becomes a ribbon and railings stripe both sides.

label: Over Menu
clause: Shoot over an open menu so cardstock becomes a foreground wall and a waiter or guest sits in the remaining slot.
